items.title: The Architecture of Craft: ArchDaily's August Editorial Focus
items.content_html:
🎨 🔧 🏔️ ✏️

When Francis Kéré set out to build a school in his home village of Gando, Burkina Faso, he chose clay, a material his own community associated with scarcity, not architecture. To prove it could hold, he built test bricks and submerged one in water for five days before showing his neighbors it hadn't failed. Then he trained the villagers themselves to raise the walls, rather than bringing in a construction crew from the city. More than 200 people from Gando have since worked as builders because of that choice. The school carries something a materials list alone cannot: the trace of the hands that will go on living in the village long after the scaffolding came down.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Machida Station Area Community Hub “Hatmachida” / Nikken Sekkei
items.content_html: As the importance of walkable urban environments continues to gain global attention, 'hatmachida' represents a practical urban strategy that inserts a compact 22.7 m² architectural intervention into a corner of a major thoroughfare as a catalyst for public activity. By deliberately positioning a small yet active presence within the city fabric, the project seeks to generate ripple effects across surrounding districts. Architecture that evolves through sustained use over time questions conventional approaches to urban renewal and proposes an alternative model for shaping cities in the years ahead.
